messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Elevated TLS handshake failures at edge-gateway (frontdoor) — 5xx spike. metric: tls.handshake_fail_rate = 18% last 5m, baseline 0.3%.

maria: @here seeing paging in the SRE channel, grabbing it. I'm oncall. starting timeline capture.

sam: I'm in. any initial indicators? errors show `ssl handshake error: OCSPResponderError` in edge logs.

tiago: getting a stack of client-side TLS errors too: `tls: handshake failure` from our gateway to upstreams (backend CA validation). Possibly a CA rotation / OCSP responder outage.

maria: scope — customer-facing API traffic dropping with 502/523/525 (gateway TLS). Some users behind strict mTLS see immediate disconnects.

jen: Support report — 3 enterprise customers reported failures (calls failing with 5xx). Raising P0 for potential SLA impact.

sam: reproduction snippet from edge node:
``
Apr 12 03:41:12 edge-3 nginx[2345]: [error] 12345#0: *98765 SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:14094412:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure) while SSL handshaking, client: 10.1.2.3
Apr 12 03:41:12 edge-3 app[2345]: ocsp stapling: responder timeout for cert id abc123
``

maria: immediate mitigations to try — (1) failover to secondary OCSP responder, (2) bypass OCSP stapling on edge for incoming client TLS (temp), (3) route critical customers to dedicated gateway pool with cached OCSP responses.

tiago: I'm checking OCSP responder latency/health. pinging ...

tiago: OCSP responder in eu-west is flapping, 504s from our health check — looks like upstream CA's OCSP service visible issue.

sam: are certs actually expired? run `openssl x509 -noout -dates -in cert.pem` on the problem chain.

maria: checked: cert dates valid. Root/issuing CA is fine. problem is OCSP responder failing, and our stapling timeout is causing handshake aborts on some clients.

jen: customer impact list: corp-alpha, corp-beta, and partner-gamma. corp-alpha on Dedicated -> fewer errors. corp-beta on Hosted -> heavy failures.

maria: action: I'm going to enable backup OCSP responder and extend stapling timeout. tiago, coordinate with infra to flip backup.

tiago: flipping backup now (edge config update staged). will post when applied.

support-bot: Deploy started by tiago: `edge-config:ocsp-fallback=true` — CI job 7682.

sam: while that deploy completes, can we create route to bypass stapling for hosts with strict failures? we can set `ssl_stapling on|off` per vhost.

maria: agreed — execute per-vhost disable for affected hostnames as a short-term mitigation. jen, can you notify customers about possible reconnection attempts and advise retrying?

jen: drafting message: "We're investigating intermittent TLS errors affecting some API calls. Short-term mitigations in progress, no cert expiry. We'll update in 30m." Will send to affected contacts now.

tiago: deploy finished. edge nodes report `ocsp fallback responder=ocsp-backup.internal:80` and stapling timeout increased to 5s.

sam: metrics look better — handshake_fail_rate down from 18% -> 4% over last 2m. still above baseline but improving.

maria: start a rolling restart on two busiest edge nodes to clear stuck connections. doing node-2 and node-4 first.

tiago: restart done. node-2 shows successful handshakes now.

maria: oncall handoff at 04:22 — @sam taking next shift for monitoring. I'm leaving notes in the incident runbook.

sam: taking over. will keep watch for 30m and coordinate with CA vendor for OCSP SLA/backup.

jen: customers notified. one corp-beta engineer replied: "we see traffic recovering, thanks".

support-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0412-OCSP (severity P1). Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0412-OCSP

maria: retrospective notes: investigate why OCSP fallback wasn't hot, review our `ssl_stapling` defaults, add circuit-breaker to routing if OCSP responder latency spikes.

sam: agreed. assign action items: tiago -> CA vendor contact + add monitoring; eng-infra -> make OCSP fallback default; security -> risk review of temporary stapling disable.

maria: closing thread for active mitigation. monitor and reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
